picks.file: Algérie.Sétif.Place de la Porte de Biskra.jpg
picks.what: Market day on the Place de la Porte de Biskra, postcard
picks.why: best of the postcards: the main square by the Biskra gate with its arcaded building and market crowd; caption and handwriting trimmed

gaps: P0–P3: nothing (a shell plate only); P5: only street scenes, a hotel, domino players, an interior and RAF planes; P6: only mountain scenery outside the city and a portrait-format street seen from a hotel
notes: No true general view of Sétif exists among the candidates. #5 is a square scene, not a panorama. Alternatives: #6 (Porte de Bougie, the gate half hidden by trees, 1900s) and #9 (Leo Wehrli, Avenue Georges Clémenceau, 1935, sharp but a plain avenue; could fill P5 if the reviewer accepts a street scene: trim [0.085, 0.055, 0.925, 0.86]). #2 shows the Ain El Fouara fountain, but only as one of four small photos on an album page, too small to trim to.
